title: The SDLC Is Out of Balance: Beyond the AI Code Review Bottleneck
summary: AI code review is one part of a wider SDLC imbalance. Local automation can move costs, weaken shared understanding and delay business returns. Rebalance the whole delivery system.

assets.caption: Machine-speed production does not automatically expand the capacity needed to own the result.

assets.alt: A lifecycle workstream sits above a before-and-after comparison. Before, generation, review and integration each handle eight comparable changes per month, with no backlog growth. After coding accelerates, generation reaches 100 while review and integration remain at eight; admitting all 100 adds 92 waiting changes per month.
assets.caption: Figure 1. One faster stage, unchanged downstream capacity. This is a thought experiment, not measured AI productivity. Comparable changes per month; all generated work admitted; no rework or other departures assumed.
assets.credit: Original explanatory diagram by Vitalii Oborskyi. CC BY 4.0. Conceptual illustration; source distinctions are stated in the caption.

assets.alt: Code review has two complementary paths. Verification produces evidence about the proposed change. Knowledge transfer supports shared understanding, which helps enable competent ownership and the ability to maintain, diagnose and recover the system.
assets.caption: Figure 2. Review supports verification and learning. Review functions: Bacchelli and Bird (2013). The links to competent ownership, maintenance and recovery are the author’s synthesis.
assets.credit: Original diagram by Vitalii Oborskyi. Review functions: Bacchelli and Bird (2013); ownership and recovery links: author systems synthesis. CC BY 4.0.

assets.alt: A conceptual time graph compares generation capacity with team understanding capacity, both expressed as comparable changes per month. The potential gap illustrates a workflow whose learning mechanisms have not kept pace.
assets.caption: Figure 3. A potential comprehension gap when generation scales faster than the team’s learning mechanisms. Illustrative capacities, not measurements or a forecast.
